title: Cave Wall Painting — An idea becomes a connected system

scenes.title: Torch-lit limestone chamber: pigment on relief
scenes.purpose: A red hand stencil (the idea) leads through finger dots to a bison and a horse. Charcoal lines and red nodes then link them into a connected system, painted onto uneven grey limestone and lit by a single torch.
visuals: Fixed procedural grey limestone #7E7B72 with deep fissures #4E4B44, calcite flowstone streaks #D9D5CA, ochre staining #C49B6B and chalk crust #DDD0B4
Red #984B32 sprayed negative hand stencil at left
Bison with a charcoal #3B2B21 contour and rubbed red fill; the contour bends where it crosses the rock ridge
Horse with a charcoal contour that breaks where a groove crosses it
Charcoal links and red pigment nodes joining the bison, the horse and three nodes
Modern caption panel on a calcite backing: AN IDEA BECOMES / a connected system
Disclosure: Procedural rock & pigment approximation — not archaeological footage

beats.development: Red pigment is sprayed in nine puffs around a hand, leaving the negative hand stencil on the limestone.
captions: Procedural rock & pigment approximation — not archaeological footage

beats.development: Finger dots trail toward the bison. The bison contour is drawn stroke by stroke, then red is rubbed in with diagonal passes, and the horse contour follows.
Charcoal links are drawn between the bison, the horse and three red nodes, closing the system.
The torch light moves from upper left to the right while the rock stays fixed. Highlights and shadows shift across the ridge, the flowstone and the pigment.
The finished composition holds for reading.

findings: The pigment reveal runs from 0.05 to 1.8 s in short ordered strokes. The light sweep tween runs from 1.75 to 2.6 s, so the frame is settled before 2.7 s.
The caption and disclosure stay visible and static for the whole video.
justifiedHolds: A 2.6–3.0 s final hold lets the viewer read the finished composition and the caption.

notes: Refresh: this uses a scene-dependent torch-lit grey limestone background. No preview recipes were supplied, and BACKGROUND_REVIEW.json reported 0 matched sources and no contact sheets.
No Blender tools were used. The renderers are Three.js, GLSL and Canvas 2D, and GSAP owns the motion.
Only the pigment reveal and the light position animate. GSAP tweens a uniform proxy, which renders synchronously on every update and on hf-seek.
The caption font is the macOS system font Gill Sans, declared with @font-face local().
